note: [F] Deicyde/diophantine-z-q, proved; confirmed finding (stronger): card_TL_le, its hypothesis proved by uniformBadBound_holds, bounds all class primes up to N that a prime l > L makes bad by A(3 log 4)/(L log L) N/log N + 20 N^(3/4), with A independent of L; [M]'s bad prime values of one form lie in that set (pointCount_pair, gcd_pointCount_eq, mod_four_of_dvd_cp), so the display follows with N = beta_A X, an extra 1/log L and a smaller error term. The containment is not stated as a Lean theorem.

snippet.text:
theorem mod_four_of_dvd_cp {p ℓ : ℕ} (hℓ : ℓ.Prime) (hℓ2 : ℓ ≠ 2) (hp : p.Prime) (hC : InClass p)
    (h1 : (ℓ : ℤ) ∣ cp p) (h2 : ℓ ∣ p + 1) : ℓ % 4 = 1 := by

provenance.method: mapper and verifier agents, a judge ruled; finding confirmed by two skeptics; status changed from no-match after an independent review; source of Deicyde/diophantine-z-q at its pin read, not built

evidence: [M]'s primes (p ≡ 1 mod 8, p ≡ 3 mod 7) are in InClass, pointCount_pair makes [M]'s a equal to ±c_p, and mod_four_of_dvd_cp gives ℓ ≡ 1 mod 4, so every bad prime value lies in T_L ∩ [0, β_A X]; card_TL_le, with uniformBadBound_holds (no hypotheses, no sorry), bounds that set with A independent of L, an extra 1/log L and N^{3/4} ≤ X^{7/8}.

Every bad prime value is in TL L: same class, same twists, and an odd ℓ dividing both orders divides c_p and p + 1 (pointCount_pair, gcd_pointCount_eq), ℓ ≡ 1 mod 4 (mod_four_of_dvd_cp). card_TL_le's bound is at least as strong, with A and N₁ chosen before L; no per-form statement exists in [F].
